decisions.reason: This broad dietary supplement line fits closely with the firm's existing portfolio and, given its strong in-house development and manufacturing capabilities, management would expect to learn and improve rather than withdraw it.

The skin and hair supplement is a related consumer-health extension with visible launch support, so a large pharmaceutical firm with its own R&D would be inclined to retain it and build on existing knowledge.

The joint-health supplement is clearly adjacent to the firm's established offer, and the firm's absorptive capacity makes it likely to keep the product while refining marketing and formulation based on early feedback.

Although the mushroom-based immune supplement is somewhat more niche and uncertain, it still builds on the firm's established supplement business, so management is more likely to keep it than exit quickly.

Because this generic blood pressure product is described as distant from the firm's established offer and already showed an early problem signal, management would see weaker ability to interpret and correct setbacks and would be relatively likely to discontinue it.
